waves.name: Nightly batch cycle
waves.rationale: All three jobs run only IEFBR14 and touch no dataset, so one family describes them. The wrapper submits JOBA then JOBB (scripts/nightly.sh:4, scripts/nightly.sh:5) and is the must-not-break item. JOBC is retired per scripts/nightly.sh:2 and its submit is commented out at scripts/nightly.sh:6. It is kept in the wave only so the unit is accounted for. If the client confirms it is retired, retire it instead of porting it. The wave is sound as one unit because the order JOBA then JOBB is the only coupling and it lives in the wrapper. Nothing in the tree shows what the cycle really does, since IEFBR14 is a no-op (jcl/JOBA.jcl:2), so the real work is either outside the tree or nothing (inference).
waves.unblocks: Nothing inside this tree. It is the whole system, so the wave is a chore until the client supplies the real nightly programs, datasets and scheduler. It does prove the wrapper-ordering and job-failure semantics that any later wave must keep.
